full_judgment: 4. The preemptees-opposite parties No.1-4 contested the case by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the case is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the case is barred by limitation and the case is barred by the principle of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence. Their case, in brief, is that the case land originally belonged to Upendra Kumar Bhoumik and Manindra Kumar Bhoumik. Subsequently, Manindra Kumar Bhoumik became the owner of the case land measuring 36 decimal through family amicable settlement. Later on, he transferred the said land to the opposite party No.5 by a sale deed. Thereafter, the opposite party No.5 transferred the case land to the opposite parties No.1-4 by Sale Deed No.10466 dated 26.10.1997 within the very knowledge of the preemptors. Prior to the said transfer the vendor-opposite party No.5 had asked all the co-sharer tenants and the tenants holding land contiguous to the case land whether they would purchase the case land but all of them had denied to purchase the same. The opposite parties No.1-4 purchased the case land for the purpose of construction of a dwelling house and after purchase they had made improvement work thereon spending of Tk.1,25,000.00. The preemptors are not entitled to pre-empt the case land and as such the pre-emption case is liable to be rejected.
